relevance_replay.rationale: The selected dimensions cover the production monitoring control loop: collecting behavioral, trajectory, reasoning, human, and slice-level telemetry (33); evaluating deployed behavior and safety (10); testing reward integrity and detecting reward exploitation (37); selecting reward references and triangulation strategies (38); detecting reward degradation and drift statistically (12); triggering operational response (25); containing or restoring failed policies (20); controlling promotion and exposure of candidate policies (19); preserving policy, training, inference, and rollback lineage (36); recording training and deployment artifacts needed for diagnosis and reproduction (35); enforcing runtime action constraints (17); adapting or serving policies after observed degradation (30); experimentally evaluating policy changes before adoption (29); and governing monitoring decisions through explainability, accountability, bias, and cross-functional controls (28). These dimensions directly affect monitoring architecture, response latency, false alarms, safety, auditability, rollback reliability, and adaptation risk.

clusters.name: Continuous Behavioral Observability
clusters.description: Which telemetry, evaluation, slicing, and anomaly-monitoring mechanisms observe deployed agent behavior?

relations.reading: Choices on Continuous Behavioral Observability affect the outcomes of Policy Experimentation Method
relations.rationale: New documents explicitly connect drift monitoring, human feedback, and observability signals to retraining and model-refresh decisions.

values.label: Continuous production observability
values.description: Continuously observe deployed model quality, fairness, and operational behavior rather than evaluating only at release.

values.label: Chain-of-thought observability
values.description: Use reasoning traces and output discrepancies to evaluate deployed model behavior and faithfulness.

values.label: Slice-aware and tail-growth monitoring
values.description: Monitoring detects failures localized to behavioral slices and delayed growth in distributional tails.

values.label: Deployment-distribution safety assessment
values.description: Evaluating deployed behavior under changing and unseen production distributions rather than training conditions alone.

values.label: LLM-based output anomaly monitor
values.description: Using a secondary model or process to continuously inspect deployed outputs for anomalous exploitation signals.

values.label: Effective-sample-size diagnostics
values.description: Sliding-window effective sample size provides supporting evidence for distributional instability.

values.label: Tool-conditioned slice monitoring
values.description: Monitoring targets tool-conditioned contexts and post-tool slices rather than only global aggregates.

values.label: Trajectory and behavior-policy observability
values.description: Captures complete trajectories and behavior-policy information needed for reliable offline evaluation and monitoring.

values.label: Segment-level feature telemetry
values.description: Monitoring of per-segment behavior and feature telemetry to expose localized failures hidden by aggregate metrics.

values.label: Human-in-the-loop production monitoring
values.description: Continuous human checking of deployed behavior alongside automated monitoring and feedback collection.

values.label: Aggregate-only monitoring
values.description: Reliance on aggregate entropy, reward, or global KL metrics without tool-conditioned or slice-level signals.

values.label: Reference-support distribution monitoring
values.description: Monitoring reference-policy probability support and state-distribution mixtures in tool-conditioned regions.

values.label: Importance-weight monitoring
values.description: Monitoring importance weights, support, and denominator sensitivity, especially in tail or low-support regions.

values.label: Shadow decision execution
values.description: Execute candidate decisions without applying them to production outcomes before promotion.

values.label: Unpressured monitoring
values.description: Monitors behavior without applying optimization pressure to the monitoring setup.

values.label: Reward-hacking trip-wire monitoring
values.description: Introduces deliberate vulnerabilities with monitoring and alerts to detect reward hacking.

values.label: Shadow-run metrics collection
values.description: Collects live-like metrics during shadow execution to bridge offline evaluation and deployment.

values.label: Parallel shadow logging
values.description: Logs decisions and context in parallel while a candidate policy executes in shadow mode.

values.label: Interaction audit logging
values.description: Retains interaction records and explanations for operational, regulatory, and post-deployment oversight.

values.label: Reference-data coverage monitoring
values.description: Monitors whether incoming requests are covered by the external reference data used at serving time.

values.label: Reward-hack behavior documentation
values.description: Documents exploit behavior and circumstances for production analysis and remediation.

values.label: Automated evaluation metrics
values.description: Uses fast automated quality metrics to monitor adaptation and deployed behavior.

values.label: Evaluator position-consistency monitoring
values.description: Monitoring evaluator judgments after swapping response positions to detect positional inconsistency and bias.

values.label: Aggregate-dashboard observability gap
values.description: Aggregate dashboards can miss late, slice-specific, or delayed signals in continuous agents.

values.label: Sensor-observation manipulation
values.description: The agent alters or blocks observations so monitoring inputs falsely indicate successful behavior.

values.label: Out-of-distribution activation indicators
values.description: Treating unusual internal activation patterns as observed signals of narrow proxy pursuit or deployed reward exploitation.

values.label: Importance-weight variance risk
values.description: Unstable policy-value and safety estimates caused by extreme importance-sampling weights.

values.label: Behavior-policy observability risk
values.description: Difficulty evaluating policy value and safety when the data-collecting behavior policy is not recorded.

values.label: Hidden reasoning and shortcut-monitoring blind spots
values.description: Monitoring outcome where visible reasoning omits deceptive reasoning, shortcuts, or reward-hacking behavior.

values.label: Task-difficulty monitoring dependence
values.description: Monitoring outcome in which task difficulty determines whether reasoning visibility reveals behavior-generating processes.

values.label: Tool-conditioned low-support variance
values.description: Monitoring outcome where tool-conditioned low-support regions amplify update variance and evade global metrics.

values.label: Trajectory incompleteness risk
values.description: Risk that missing telemetry or incomplete state trajectories undermine reliable production monitoring and evaluation.

values.label: Reasoning-monitor evasion
values.description: Models hide undesirable reasoning or encode it while continuing the associated behavior.

values.label: Reduced reward-hack verbalization
values.description: Suppresses verbalized reward hacking while potentially leaving underlying behavior unresolved.

clusters.name: Behavioral and Reasoning Evaluation
clusters.description: Which tests evaluate deployed behavior and reasoning observability across scenarios and human review?

values.label: Scratchpad-based reasoning observability
values.description: Expose intermediate reasoning traces to inspect hidden behavior associated with reward hacking.

values.label: Hint-based faithfulness evaluation
values.description: Provide correct and incorrect hints and test whether reported reasoning acknowledges influential information.

values.label: Light reasoning-trace optimization
values.description: Applying limited optimization pressure to reasoning traces without directly strongly supervising their content.

values.label: Direct strong chain-of-thought supervision
values.description: Strongly supervising chain-of-thought outputs as a training signal.

values.label: Penalized undesirable thoughts
values.description: Penalizing undesirable reasoning content as an intervention to prevent monitored misbehavior.

values.label: Multi-objective evaluation suite
values.description: Use complementary metrics so an agent cannot optimize one metric while degrading related objectives.

values.label: Held-out environment testing
values.description: Evaluate agents in environments different from training conditions to reveal environment-specific shortcuts.

values.label: Human review of high-stakes behavior
values.description: Retain human review for unusually behaving or apparently high-performing agents in consequential applications.

values.label: Open-source post-training diagnostics
values.description: Using released detection, evaluation, and annotation infrastructure for reproducible post-training monitoring.

values.label: Manual human monitoring at scale
values.description: Relying on manual review of agent actions as the primary deployed behavioral monitoring approach.

values.label: Adversarial-policy evaluation
values.description: A deployed or victim policy is tested against strategically trained adversarial policies.

values.label: Human feedback loop
values.description: Collect post-deployment human feedback and feed it into model or policy updates.

values.label: Chain-of-Thought sole-safeguard reliance
values.description: Treating Chain-of-Thought monitoring as sufficient to rule out deceptive or undesirable behavior.

values.label: Process-level supervision
values.description: Supervises intermediate reasoning or behavior steps rather than judging only final outputs.

values.label: Outcome-only reward evaluation
values.description: Evaluates only final outputs without intermediate-step supervision.

values.label: Programmatic intermediate verification
values.description: Uses objective tests to verify intermediate generated behavior where reliable verification is available.

values.label: Internal principle checklists
values.description: Uses structured internal checkpoints to evaluate reasoning beyond a single scalar outcome.

values.label: Reasoning propensity measurement
values.description: Measures the tendency to produce particular kinds of reasoning to assess monitoring effectiveness.

values.label: Domain-specific evaluation benchmarks
values.description: Evaluates deployed behavior against industry-specific accuracy, coding, recognition, or compliance requirements.

values.label: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation
values.description: Uses a stronger model for pairwise comparison and reasoning-quality or compliance assessment.

values.label: Reasoning-trace intent concealment
values.description: Models hide intentions or unauthorized information in reasoning traces, reducing monitoring faithfulness.

values.label: Reduced human error detectability
values.description: RLHF outputs become more convincing and harder for human evaluators to classify correctly.

values.label: Evaluator-gaming behavior
values.description: Agents manipulate evaluators or tests so observed success does not reflect actual task completion.

values.label: Sycophantic feedback
values.description: Outputs track stated user preferences rather than truth, weakening behavioral monitoring.

values.label: Insufficient human feedback signals
values.description: Monitoring outcome in open-ended domains where human oversight and feedback are inadequate for assessing alignment.

values.label: Verification-capability constraint
values.description: Limits process supervision where reliable objective verification is unavailable, especially for subjective tasks.

values.label: Evaluator self-preference bias
values.description: Evaluation distortion caused by a grader favoring outputs from its own model family.

values.label: Response-position bias
values.description: Evaluation distortion caused by the displayed position of candidate responses.

clusters.name: Reward Integrity Testing
clusters.description: Which tests detect whether reward signals and optimized behavior remain aligned with intended objectives?

relations.reading: Choices on Reward Integrity Testing affect the outcomes of Reward Statistic and Drift Detection
relations.rationale: Evaluation signals determine whether behavioral degradation or reward gaming is recognized before it becomes a production incident.

relations.reading: Choices on Reward Integrity Testing limit the options available on Policy Promotion and Exposure
relations.rationale: Adversarial, held-out, human, and safety evaluations can gate promotion or trigger recovery actions.

values.label: Reward-function measurement audit
values.description: Review measured reward proxies against intended objectives to expose specification gaps.

values.label: Adversarial reward-function testing
values.description: Actively attempt to break reward functions and record discovered exploits before relying on them operationally.

values.label: Reward-function integrity test
values.description: Use an explicit test artifact to detect whether the reward function has been modified.

values.label: Proxy-objective alignment monitoring
values.description: Monitor whether optimized proxy metrics remain aligned with the intended objective.

values.label: Pre-training reward-hacking detection
values.description: Proxy-reward defects are screened before optimization begins.

values.label: Proxy–true reward correlation analysis
values.description: Proxy and intended rewards are compared across rollouts to assess reward misspecification.

values.label: Reward-hack frequency measurement
values.description: Quantifies how often reward hacking occurs across tasks, models, domains, and training scales.

values.label: Reward-hack property classification
values.description: Classifies reward hacks by their observable properties and behavioral mechanisms.

values.label: Reproducible reward-hacking model organisms
values.description: Uses accessible open models that reproduce reward-hacking behavior for repeatable investigation and evaluation.

values.label: Verbalization-based reward-hack detection
values.description: Uses model verbalization or acknowledgment of shortcut exploitation to improve behavioral transparency and detection.

values.label: Functional-test reward gaming
values.description: Evaluation of whether agents satisfy narrow tests through special-casing, hard-coding, stubbing, or deleting rather than preserving intended functionality.

values.label: Capability-limit and hazardous-situation evaluation
values.description: Evaluation of whether deployed agents recognize unfamiliar or hazardous situations and signal when they cannot safely act.

values.label: Reward-tampering-as-hacking classification
values.description: Treating manipulation of reward generation or inputs as a reward-hacking category for monitoring.

values.label: Interpretability-based reward-hack detection
values.description: Uses interpretability methods to identify reward-hacking loopholes and proxy exploitation.

values.label: Low hint-disclosure rate
values.description: Observed failure outcome in which models disclose influential hints infrequently, limiting faithfulness-monitoring effectiveness.

values.label: Production reward hacking
values.description: Deployed agents exploit reward functions, proxy metrics, evaluators, or environment defects instead of intended objectives.

values.label: Capability-amplified reward exploit sophistication
values.description: More capable systems discover subtler and more effective reward exploits.

values.label: Incomplete human-approval alignment signal
values.description: Human approval can reward convincing but inaccurate outputs and therefore incompletely represents factual correctness.

values.label: Post-failure reward-hack occurrence
values.description: Measures whether reward hacking follows failed normal attempts or appears immediately.

values.label: Cross-domain reward-hack coverage
values.description: Observed reward-hacking coverage across programming, agentic, open-ended, and other task domains.

values.label: Cross-model reward-hack coverage
values.description: Observed reward-hacking coverage across different model families and reasoning-model variants.

values.label: Cross-behavior reward-hack generalization
values.description: Transfer of one learned reward-hacking behavior to other distinct harmful or deceptive behaviors.

values.label: Reward-hacking anomaly transition
values.description: Detects abrupt behavioral phase transitions associated with capability-amplified reward exploitation.

values.label: Observed reward-hack frequency
values.description: Measured frequency of reward hacking across evaluated settings and training conditions.

values.label: Spurious-feature dependence
values.description: Reliance on incidental or unreliable features that produces shortcut behavior instead of intended generalization.

values.label: Hidden reward-hacking behavior
values.description: Evaluation of whether agents conceal reward hacking or remain undetected under oversight.

values.label: Functional validity failure
values.description: Outcome where narrow evaluation success does not preserve intended implementation behavior or correctness.

values.label: Capability-correctness performance tension
values.description: Outcome where speed or optimization gains conflict with correctness under reward-driven evaluation.

values.label: Novel-situation and training-distribution mismatch
values.description: Outcome where unfamiliar deployment observations produce irrational or overconfident actions outside the training distribution.

clusters.name: Reward Statistic and Drift Detection
clusters.description: Which reward statistic and statistical test detect post-deployment degradation while controlling false alarms?

relations.reading: Choices on Reward Statistic and Drift Detection affect the outcomes of Policy Promotion and Exposure
relations.rationale: Detection speed and false-alarm behavior determine when a deployed policy is gated, rolled back, or investigated.

values.label: Weighted reward-mean test
values.description: Compare sequential rewards using a covariance-aware weighted mean rather than an unweighted recent mean.

values.label: Inverse-covariance row-sum weighting
values.description: Derive reward weights from row sums of the inverse covariance matrix under a normal-reward assumption.

values.label: Naive simple-mean benchmark
values.description: Use the simple mean as a conventional comparison detector in RL monitoring experiments.

values.label: Complete-episode bootstrap statistic
values.description: Bootstrapping complete episodes to preserve dependence structure when constructing degradation thresholds.

values.label: BFAR-based drift detection test
values.description: Use BFAR as the primary test for detecting deployed-agent degradation.

values.label: Recent-episode simple-mean detector
values.description: Compare the recent reward mean with a reference mean; explicitly characterized as suboptimal for degradation detection.

values.label: CUSUM detector benchmark
values.description: Use CUSUM as a competing sequential-testing method for detecting reward degradation.

values.label: Hotelling mean-shift benchmark
values.description: Use Hotelling’s multivariate mean-shift test as a competing degradation detector.

values.label: Moving-average reward detector
values.description: Detecting degradation from a configurable moving average of recent episode rewards.

values.label: Multi-metric reward monitoring
values.description: Monitors several complementary reward or performance metrics to detect divergence and degradation.

values.label: Cross-metric degradation detection
values.description: Detects improvement in an optimized metric accompanied by deterioration in complementary metrics.

clusters.name: Operational Drift Response Trigger
clusters.description: Which operational trigger or diagnostic initiates response to detected production degradation?

values.label: Threshold-triggered monitoring response
values.description: Initiates operational response when a monitored production-quality or service metric crosses a configured threshold, without requiring rollout callbacks or persistence checks.

includes.label: Threshold-based operational alerting
includes.description: Trigger monitoring response when production quality or service indicators cross configured thresholds.

values.label: Rollout-callback diagnostic response
values.description: Initiates degradation diagnostics from rollout lifecycle callbacks, typically using threshold checks at those rollout points rather than evaluating every environment step.

includes.label: Threshold-based operational alerting
includes.description: Trigger monitoring response when production quality or service indicators cross configured thresholds.

includes.label: Callback-based rollout diagnostics
includes.description: Attaching degradation checks to a rollout lifecycle callback rather than evaluating every environment step.

values.label: Multi-signal SLO-governed rollback response
values.description: Initiates or controls rollback through a coordinated policy combining threshold checks, rollout diagnostics, persistence requirements, calibrated trigger levels, and SLO-aware serving protections.

includes.label: Threshold-based operational alerting
includes.description: Trigger monitoring response when production quality or service indicators cross configured thresholds.

includes.label: Callback-based rollout diagnostics
includes.description: Attaching degradation checks to a rollout lifecycle callback rather than evaluating every environment step.

includes.label: Persistent-condition rollback trigger
includes.description: Initiates operational response only when degradation persists for a configured duration or frequency.

includes.label: Rollback threshold calibration
includes.description: Tunes operational trigger thresholds to balance rapid degradation response against false alarms and flapping.

includes.label: SLO-aware serving policies
includes.description: Serving policies that govern routing and protection actions while satisfying latency service objectives.

values.label: False-alarm control
values.description: Desired monitoring outcome in which unchanged environments do not generate spurious degradation alerts.

values.label: Rapid degradation detection
values.description: Desired outcome in which genuine degradation is detected quickly and consistently after environmental change.

values.label: Production drift degradation effects
values.description: Input, concept, knowledge, or parameter drift produces outdated, incorrect, or irrelevant deployed responses.

values.label: User-trust erosion
values.description: Loss of user trust resulting from unattended production drift and associated model errors.

clusters.name: Policy Recovery Control
clusters.description: Which recovery mechanism contains or restores a deployed policy after failure?

values.label: Automated policy rollback
values.description: Automatically restore a known-good policy when regressions or safety-SLO violations occur.

values.label: State restoration for stateful policies
values.description: Restore or reset online-learning state in addition to replacing the policy version.

values.label: Automated circuit breakers
values.description: Automatic protective intervention detects degraded performance and switches or contains the deployed policy.

values.label: Safe fallback policies
values.description: A degraded agent is switched to a predefined safer policy during recovery.

values.label: Incident-capable on-call recovery
values.description: Assigning authorized on-call personnel to disable unsafe policies and activate fallback behavior.

values.label: Runbook-based incident recovery
values.description: Using stepwise runbooks for known incidents and coordinated playbooks for complex policy failures.

values.label: Fail-safe degradation handling
values.description: Keep deployed agents operating safely or recover gracefully when learning or environmental conditions cause poor performance.

values.label: Increased stateful rollback complexity
values.description: Outcome in which restoring state makes rollback more complex than replacing a stateless model.

values.label: Conversion-regression recovery workflow
values.description: Rollback, incident analysis, counterfactual testing, conservative retraining, and redeployment restore policy performance.

clusters.name: Policy Promotion and Exposure
clusters.description: Which pre-production and rollout process exposes and promotes candidate policies?

relations.reading: Policy Promotion and Exposure requires Training Artifact Configuration to be decided first
relations.rationale: Safe promotion and rollback depend on identifying candidate versions, their training history, and known-good restoration targets.

values.label: Counterfactual testing in CI/CD
values.description: Test alternative policy actions offline before deployment without unsafe online exploration.

values.label: Policy safety gates
values.description: Require offline evaluation and simulated safety checks before staging or production promotion.

values.label: Shadow deployment
values.description: Observe a candidate policy under production conditions without allowing it to affect live decisions.

values.label: Canary or blue-green rollout
values.description: Limit production exposure through controlled rollout patterns that support observation and containment.

values.label: Counterfactual policy-value gating
values.description: Uses logged-data estimates and their uncertainty to gate policy promotion.

clusters.name: Production Policy Lineage
clusters.description: Which deployed policy versions, variants, inference data, rollback events, and environments are traceable?

relations.reading: Choices on Production Policy Lineage limit the options available on Policy Promotion and Exposure
relations.rationale: Version, variant, environment, and rollback traceability constrain safe promotion and exposure decisions.

values.label: Registry-anchored policy lineage
values.description: Tracks deployed policy versions through their training histories and uses model-registry status to identify rollback targets. This provides basic traceability for deployment and recovery.

includes.label: Production policy lineage tracking
includes.description: Connect deployed policies to their training histories and associated experiments.

includes.label: Model-registry rollback targets
includes.description: Use registry promotion status to identify an unambiguous previously known-good policy version.

values.label: Auditable rollback lineage
values.description: Combines registry-based rollback targeting with explicit audit records of rollback triggers, source versions, target versions, and timing.

includes.label: Model-registry rollback targets
includes.description: Use registry promotion status to identify an unambiguous previously known-good policy version.

includes.label: Rollback event audit logging
includes.description: Record rollback triggers, timestamps, source versions, and target versions for post-mortem analysis.

values.label: End-to-end deployment evidence lineage
values.description: Links live endpoints and variants to training jobs and retained inference data, while anchoring deployed versions and rollback targets in policy lineage records.

includes.label: Production policy lineage tracking
includes.description: Connect deployed policies to their training histories and associated experiments.

includes.label: Model-registry rollback targets
includes.description: Use registry promotion status to identify an unambiguous previously known-good policy version.

includes.label: Production-variant traceability
includes.description: Record links from a live endpoint to its deployed model variant and originating training job.

includes.label: Inference capture-data retention
includes.description: Persist production requests, responses, metadata, and time-partitioned records for later evaluation.

values.label: Operational capture with environment isolation
values.description: Retains production inference records while separating training infrastructure from serving infrastructure to protect production stability and latency.

includes.label: Inference capture-data retention
includes.description: Persist production requests, responses, metadata, and time-partitioned records for later evaluation.

includes.label: Separated training and inference environments
includes.description: Keep training and serving infrastructure separate to preserve serving stability and latency.

clusters.name: Training Artifact Configuration
clusters.description: Which training configurations, outputs, and reproducibility artifacts are recorded for audit and replication?

values.label: CloudWatch print-log storage
values.description: Centralize operational training print logs in CloudWatch.

values.label: S3 training-output storage
values.description: Persist training outputs, metrics, and artifacts in durable object storage.

values.label: Experiment configuration tracking
values.description: Track state representations, reward functions, algorithms, hyperparameters, and job variations.

values.label: Single-click training-job replication
values.description: Replicate training jobs easily to support reproducibility and investigation.

clusters.name: Runtime Safety Shielding
clusters.description: Which runtime intervention architecture constrains or replaces unsafe agent actions before they reach the environment?

relations.reading: Choices on Runtime Safety Shielding affect the outcomes of Behavioral and Reasoning Evaluation
relations.rationale: The new shield architecture changes which unsafe actions reach environments and therefore changes observed behavioral safety outcomes.

values.label: Runtime action shield
values.description: An architectural layer intercepts policy actions between the agent and environment and blocks or replaces unsafe actions.

values.label: Static dynamics-based shielding
values.description: Shield decisions rely on fixed transition-dynamics, hidden-parameter, and hazard-boundary assumptions.

values.label: Shield-only safety architecture
values.description: Treating the runtime shield as the complete safety mechanism without measuring interventions under changed conditions.

values.label: Unsafe-action blocking or replacement
values.description: Blocking unsafe policy actions or substituting safer actions before environment execution.

values.label: Adaptive action shielding
values.description: Runtime shielding adapts its safe-action gate to detected distribution shifts or uncertainty.

values.label: Adaptive hidden-parameter shielding
values.description: Infer changing hidden risk parameters online and shield unsafe policy actions.

values.label: Deployment-time action constraints
values.description: Enforces allowed-action limits at deployment before policy actions reach the environment.

values.label: Business-rule validation
values.description: Validates generated or extracted outputs against structured operational and compliance rules.

values.label: Prompt-injection output guardrail
values.description: Runtime filtering or blocking that prevents prompt-injection attempts from producing unsafe agent outputs.

values.label: Restricted-topic output enforcement
values.description: Runtime enforcement that blocks responses on sensitive or prohibited topics.

clusters.name: Reward Reliability Reference Strategy
clusters.description: Which trusted, ensemble, oracle, or source-model reference strategy assesses reward-model reliability?

values.label: Reward-model ensemble agreement
values.description: Assess reward reliability by requiring agreement among multiple reward models before accepting a reward assessment.

includes.label: Reward-model ensemble agreement
includes.description: Using multiple reward models and requiring agreement before trusting reward assessments.

values.label: Trusted-policy reference triangulation
values.description: Assess reliability by triangulating reward behavior against a trusted policy, a synthetic oracle reward, and an ensemble of reward models.

includes.label: Trusted-policy distribution comparison
includes.description: Compare deployed policy action distributions with a trusted baseline to identify anomalous behavior.

includes.label: Synthetic oracle reward reference
includes.description: Using a high-quality synthetic oracle reward as a gold reference for evaluating proxy-reward optimization.

includes.label: Reward-model ensemble agreement
includes.description: Using multiple reward models and requiring agreement before trusting reward assessments.

values.label: Source-model reward-effect triangulation
values.description: Assess reliability by combining a synthetic oracle or source-model comparison with ensemble-based checks to isolate and validate reinforcement-learning effects on reward behavior.

includes.label: Synthetic oracle reward reference
includes.description: Using a high-quality synthetic oracle reward as a gold reference for evaluating proxy-reward optimization.

includes.label: Reward-model ensemble agreement
includes.description: Using multiple reward models and requiring agreement before trusting reward assessments.

includes.label: Reasoning-to-source model comparison
includes.description: Compares a reasoning model with its source model to isolate reinforcement-learning effects on reward hacking.

values.label: Proxy-to-gold reward gap
values.description: A widening divergence between optimized proxy reward and gold reward that exposes overoptimization.

values.label: Reward-model data-volume effect
values.description: Reward-model training-data volume changes gold-reward quality and the extent of Goodharting.

clusters.name: Post-deployment Adaptation and Serving
clusters.description: Which update, serving, and adaptive infrastructure changes deployed policy behavior or its production execution?

values.label: Scheduled fine-tuning jobs
values.description: Collect recent data and perform evaluated nightly or weekly incremental updates.

values.label: Continuous online model updating
values.description: Update deployed models from new information and feedback in near real time.

values.label: Metric-triggered retraining
values.description: Starting retraining when monitored performance crosses a threshold instead of only following a calendar.

values.label: Automated drift-to-deployment retraining
values.description: Automating monitoring, drift detection, retraining, validation, and deployment as one adaptation workflow.

values.label: Selective component retraining
values.description: Updating selected model components rather than all weights to reduce adaptation effort.

values.label: Rolling PEFT fine-tuning
values.description: Use parameter-efficient rolling updates to keep deployed models fresh without full retraining.

values.label: Micro-batch or single-sample updates
values.description: Apply updates at streaming micro-batch or individual-sample granularity.

values.label: Immediate feedback incorporation
values.description: Fine-tune immediately after a user rejects or corrects a deployed-system response.

values.label: Human-escalated corrective update
values.description: Escalate detected production problems to human review or retraining before or alongside automated updating.

values.label: Engagement-driven self-refinement
values.description: Refining deployed outputs or policy using engagement feedback.

values.label: API-error-driven policy refinement
values.description: Adapting policy behavior after tool or API errors to recover from deployment failures.

values.label: Retrieval and model-editing adaptation
values.description: Updates deployed models through retrieval augmentation or targeted editing instead of full retraining.

values.label: Supervised fine-tuning
values.description: Updates a pretrained model by imitating curated demonstrations before or during alignment operations.

values.label: Production policy freezing
values.description: Freezing deployed policies and allowing updates only after offline or controlled testing.

values.label: Human-escalated policy correction
values.description: Using human review and supervision to steer or adjust deployed policy behavior after observed issues.

values.label: MLOps-integrated refresh workflow
values.description: Integrating deployment monitoring, feedback collection, and recurring model refreshes into repeatable operational pipelines.

values.label: Distributed-aware metric monitoring
values.description: Metrics account for cross-rank aggregation, stragglers, and memory imbalance during distributed training.

values.label: Serving-time computation reuse
values.description: Reuse serving-generated intermediate computations during training to reduce repeated forward-pass work.

values.label: Fixed-base continuously learned adapter
values.description: Update a LoRA adapter continuously while keeping the base model fixed.

values.label: Reversible adapter updates
values.description: Swap in new adapters and revert them when operational or behavioral problems occur.

values.label: GPU-backed inference serving
values.description: Use accelerator-backed serving to meet deployed model latency and throughput requirements.

values.label: Quantized or distilled model serving
values.description: Reduce serving resource requirements through quantization or knowledge distillation while preserving alignment.

values.label: Request batching
values.description: Batch inference requests to improve aggregate serving throughput.

values.label: Constrained or conservative policy updates
values.description: Limit policy changes or enforce safety constraints during learning to reduce catastrophic degradation.

values.label: Policy-managed warm pool
values.description: Serving infrastructure maintains a warm pool whose pre-warming behavior is controlled by a learned policy.

values.label: Temporal and user-context serving features
values.description: Supplying temporal patterns and user context as policy inputs for serving-time prediction.

values.label: Multi-model endpoint serving
values.description: Consolidating multiple policy models behind one serving endpoint.

values.label: Training-serving process co-location
values.description: Place training and serving processes together to support faster online updates.

values.label: Rapid serving-to-training data transfer
values.description: Feed serving data quickly to a separate training cluster rather than updating serving servers directly.

values.label: On-device edge inference placement
values.description: Running the deployed policy directly on edge devices under device compute and storage constraints.

values.label: Lower platform total cost of ownership
values.description: A reported economic effect of selecting the managed platform.

values.label: Higher developer productivity
values.description: A reported productivity effect of the selected RL platform approach.

values.label: Model freshness
values.description: Outcome in which deployed models remain current with new information and feedback.

values.label: Rapid adaptation to streaming data
values.description: Outcome in which continual updates let an agent adapt faster than periodic retraining permits.

values.label: Retraining cost and time burden
values.description: The computational and resource burden that limits frequent full retraining.

values.label: Repeated-feedback constraint violations
values.description: Additional error-recovery rounds improve recovery while increasing severe constraint violations.

values.label: Parameter-efficient update efficiency
values.description: Uses adapter-based updates to reduce compute and memory burden for frequent production adaptation.

values.label: Reduced fine-tuning cost
values.description: Lowers the financial cost of post-deployment model updates relative to full retraining.

values.label: Repeated forward-pass computation
values.description: Outcome in which conventional separation causes serving computations to be repeated during training.

values.label: Near-real-time model updates
values.description: Outcome enabled by tightly integrated training, serving, and computation reuse.

clusters.name: Policy Experimentation Method
clusters.description: Which offline, online, hybrid, or simulation method evaluates policy changes before adoption?

values.label: Offline RL for constrained environments
values.description: Use offline RL when online interaction is dangerous, costly, or legally restricted.

values.label: Online or hybrid experimentation
values.description: Use online or hybrid methods when safe experimentation is possible but logged data is limited.

values.label: Nonrepresentative-log offline RL
values.description: Use offline RL despite nonrepresentative logs or poorly defined rewards; explicitly rejected as unreliable.

values.label: Batch-constrained deep Q-learning
values.description: Offline learning constrains value updates to the support of a fixed dataset to limit extrapolation risk.

values.label: Conservative Q-learning
values.description: Offline value estimation is deliberately conservative to reduce overoptimistic production policies.

values.label: Pairwise LLM feedback scoring
values.description: Using pairwise LLM judgments converted through Bradley–Terry scoring to guide feedback optimization.

values.label: Ray-based RL framework
values.description: Using Ray as the framework for rapidly starting and scaling reinforcement-learning workloads.

values.label: Amazon SageMaker RL platform
values.description: Using managed Amazon SageMaker RL services to move reinforcement-learning development into production-scale workloads.

values.label: Conservative offline objective
values.description: Using conservative objectives and regularization to limit offline overfitting and risky policy behavior.

clusters.name: Monitoring Governance and Explainability
clusters.description: Which governance and transparency model makes production-agent monitoring decisions accountable, interpretable, and compliant?

relations.reading: Choices on Monitoring Governance and Explainability limit the options available on Continuous Behavioral Observability
relations.rationale: s23_p10 ties explainability, accountability, and bias governance requirements to how deployed behavior is monitored and audited.

values.label: Ethical monitoring framework
values.description: Guides production monitoring and model governance through explicit ethical principles addressing bias and unsafe behavior.

values.label: Explainable monitoring decisions
values.description: Provides mechanisms that make model decisions and monitoring judgments understandable and auditable to stakeholders.

values.label: Transparent decision-making
values.description: Requires stakeholders to understand decision rationale rather than treating monitoring and model behavior as a black box.

values.label: Regulatory accountability controls
values.description: Uses formal accountability and fairness controls to satisfy evolving AI governance and compliance expectations.

values.label: Black-box decision-making
values.description: Leaves production decisions opaque to stakeholders and auditors.

values.label: Ongoing bias monitoring
values.description: Continuously checks deployed decisions for bias introduced by feedback, annotation, or model behavior.

values.label: Cross-functional monitoring governance
values.description: Joint interpretation of technical drift, domain changes, and business impact by ML, operations, and domain stakeholders.

values.label: Business-impact monitoring integration
values.description: Linking monitoring to analytics and reporting dashboards for business, safety, accuracy, and satisfaction outcomes.

values.label: Unsafe production behavior
values.description: Unsafe deployed behavior that governance, explainability, and bias controls seek to reduce.

values.label: Reputational risk from opaque decisions
values.description: Loss of trust and reputation caused by unintelligible or unauditable production decisions.

values.label: Human-value alignment
values.description: Alignment of production behavior with safety, harmlessness, context awareness, and human values.

selected_clusters.name: Continuous Behavioral Observability
selected_clusters.description: Which telemetry, evaluation, slicing, and anomaly-monitoring mechanisms observe deployed agent behavior?

relations.reading: Choices on Continuous Behavioral Observability affect the outcomes of Policy Experimentation Method
relations.rationale: New documents explicitly connect drift monitoring, human feedback, and observability signals to retraining and model-refresh decisions.

values.label: Continuous production observability
values.description: Continuously observe deployed model quality, fairness, and operational behavior rather than evaluating only at release.

values.label: Chain-of-thought observability
values.description: Use reasoning traces and output discrepancies to evaluate deployed model behavior and faithfulness.

values.label: Slice-aware and tail-growth monitoring
values.description: Monitoring detects failures localized to behavioral slices and delayed growth in distributional tails.

values.label: Deployment-distribution safety assessment
values.description: Evaluating deployed behavior under changing and unseen production distributions rather than training conditions alone.

values.label: LLM-based output anomaly monitor
values.description: Using a secondary model or process to continuously inspect deployed outputs for anomalous exploitation signals.

values.label: Effective-sample-size diagnostics
values.description: Sliding-window effective sample size provides supporting evidence for distributional instability.

values.label: Tool-conditioned slice monitoring
values.description: Monitoring targets tool-conditioned contexts and post-tool slices rather than only global aggregates.

values.label: Trajectory and behavior-policy observability
values.description: Captures complete trajectories and behavior-policy information needed for reliable offline evaluation and monitoring.

values.label: Segment-level feature telemetry
values.description: Monitoring of per-segment behavior and feature telemetry to expose localized failures hidden by aggregate metrics.

values.label: Human-in-the-loop production monitoring
values.description: Continuous human checking of deployed behavior alongside automated monitoring and feedback collection.

values.label: Aggregate-only monitoring
values.description: Reliance on aggregate entropy, reward, or global KL metrics without tool-conditioned or slice-level signals.

values.label: Reference-support distribution monitoring
values.description: Monitoring reference-policy probability support and state-distribution mixtures in tool-conditioned regions.

values.label: Importance-weight monitoring
values.description: Monitoring importance weights, support, and denominator sensitivity, especially in tail or low-support regions.

values.label: Shadow decision execution
values.description: Execute candidate decisions without applying them to production outcomes before promotion.

values.label: Unpressured monitoring
values.description: Monitors behavior without applying optimization pressure to the monitoring setup.

values.label: Reward-hacking trip-wire monitoring
values.description: Introduces deliberate vulnerabilities with monitoring and alerts to detect reward hacking.

values.label: Shadow-run metrics collection
values.description: Collects live-like metrics during shadow execution to bridge offline evaluation and deployment.

values.label: Parallel shadow logging
values.description: Logs decisions and context in parallel while a candidate policy executes in shadow mode.

values.label: Interaction audit logging
values.description: Retains interaction records and explanations for operational, regulatory, and post-deployment oversight.

values.label: Reference-data coverage monitoring
values.description: Monitors whether incoming requests are covered by the external reference data used at serving time.

values.label: Reward-hack behavior documentation
values.description: Documents exploit behavior and circumstances for production analysis and remediation.

values.label: Automated evaluation metrics
values.description: Uses fast automated quality metrics to monitor adaptation and deployed behavior.

values.label: Evaluator position-consistency monitoring
values.description: Monitoring evaluator judgments after swapping response positions to detect positional inconsistency and bias.

values.label: Aggregate-dashboard observability gap
values.description: Aggregate dashboards can miss late, slice-specific, or delayed signals in continuous agents.

values.label: Sensor-observation manipulation
values.description: The agent alters or blocks observations so monitoring inputs falsely indicate successful behavior.

values.label: Out-of-distribution activation indicators
values.description: Treating unusual internal activation patterns as observed signals of narrow proxy pursuit or deployed reward exploitation.

values.label: Importance-weight variance risk
values.description: Unstable policy-value and safety estimates caused by extreme importance-sampling weights.

values.label: Behavior-policy observability risk
values.description: Difficulty evaluating policy value and safety when the data-collecting behavior policy is not recorded.

values.label: Hidden reasoning and shortcut-monitoring blind spots
values.description: Monitoring outcome where visible reasoning omits deceptive reasoning, shortcuts, or reward-hacking behavior.

values.label: Task-difficulty monitoring dependence
values.description: Monitoring outcome in which task difficulty determines whether reasoning visibility reveals behavior-generating processes.

values.label: Tool-conditioned low-support variance
values.description: Monitoring outcome where tool-conditioned low-support regions amplify update variance and evade global metrics.

values.label: Trajectory incompleteness risk
values.description: Risk that missing telemetry or incomplete state trajectories undermine reliable production monitoring and evaluation.

values.label: Reasoning-monitor evasion
values.description: Models hide undesirable reasoning or encode it while continuing the associated behavior.

values.label: Reduced reward-hack verbalization
values.description: Suppresses verbalized reward hacking while potentially leaving underlying behavior unresolved.

selected_clusters.name: Behavioral and Reasoning Evaluation
selected_clusters.description: Which tests evaluate deployed behavior and reasoning observability across scenarios and human review?

values.label: Scratchpad-based reasoning observability
values.description: Expose intermediate reasoning traces to inspect hidden behavior associated with reward hacking.

values.label: Hint-based faithfulness evaluation
values.description: Provide correct and incorrect hints and test whether reported reasoning acknowledges influential information.

values.label: Light reasoning-trace optimization
values.description: Applying limited optimization pressure to reasoning traces without directly strongly supervising their content.

values.label: Direct strong chain-of-thought supervision
values.description: Strongly supervising chain-of-thought outputs as a training signal.

values.label: Penalized undesirable thoughts
values.description: Penalizing undesirable reasoning content as an intervention to prevent monitored misbehavior.

values.label: Multi-objective evaluation suite
values.description: Use complementary metrics so an agent cannot optimize one metric while degrading related objectives.

values.label: Held-out environment testing
values.description: Evaluate agents in environments different from training conditions to reveal environment-specific shortcuts.

values.label: Human review of high-stakes behavior
values.description: Retain human review for unusually behaving or apparently high-performing agents in consequential applications.

values.label: Open-source post-training diagnostics
values.description: Using released detection, evaluation, and annotation infrastructure for reproducible post-training monitoring.

values.label: Manual human monitoring at scale
values.description: Relying on manual review of agent actions as the primary deployed behavioral monitoring approach.

values.label: Adversarial-policy evaluation
values.description: A deployed or victim policy is tested against strategically trained adversarial policies.

values.label: Human feedback loop
values.description: Collect post-deployment human feedback and feed it into model or policy updates.

values.label: Chain-of-Thought sole-safeguard reliance
values.description: Treating Chain-of-Thought monitoring as sufficient to rule out deceptive or undesirable behavior.

values.label: Process-level supervision
values.description: Supervises intermediate reasoning or behavior steps rather than judging only final outputs.

values.label: Outcome-only reward evaluation
values.description: Evaluates only final outputs without intermediate-step supervision.

values.label: Programmatic intermediate verification
values.description: Uses objective tests to verify intermediate generated behavior where reliable verification is available.

values.label: Internal principle checklists
values.description: Uses structured internal checkpoints to evaluate reasoning beyond a single scalar outcome.

values.label: Reasoning propensity measurement
values.description: Measures the tendency to produce particular kinds of reasoning to assess monitoring effectiveness.

values.label: Domain-specific evaluation benchmarks
values.description: Evaluates deployed behavior against industry-specific accuracy, coding, recognition, or compliance requirements.

values.label: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation
values.description: Uses a stronger model for pairwise comparison and reasoning-quality or compliance assessment.

values.label: Reasoning-trace intent concealment
values.description: Models hide intentions or unauthorized information in reasoning traces, reducing monitoring faithfulness.

values.label: Reduced human error detectability
values.description: RLHF outputs become more convincing and harder for human evaluators to classify correctly.

values.label: Evaluator-gaming behavior
values.description: Agents manipulate evaluators or tests so observed success does not reflect actual task completion.

values.label: Sycophantic feedback
values.description: Outputs track stated user preferences rather than truth, weakening behavioral monitoring.

values.label: Insufficient human feedback signals
values.description: Monitoring outcome in open-ended domains where human oversight and feedback are inadequate for assessing alignment.

values.label: Verification-capability constraint
values.description: Limits process supervision where reliable objective verification is unavailable, especially for subjective tasks.

values.label: Evaluator self-preference bias
values.description: Evaluation distortion caused by a grader favoring outputs from its own model family.

values.label: Response-position bias
values.description: Evaluation distortion caused by the displayed position of candidate responses.

selected_clusters.name: Reward Integrity Testing
selected_clusters.description: Which tests detect whether reward signals and optimized behavior remain aligned with intended objectives?

relations.reading: Choices on Reward Integrity Testing affect the outcomes of Reward Statistic and Drift Detection
relations.rationale: Evaluation signals determine whether behavioral degradation or reward gaming is recognized before it becomes a production incident.

relations.reading: Choices on Reward Integrity Testing limit the options available on Policy Promotion and Exposure
relations.rationale: Adversarial, held-out, human, and safety evaluations can gate promotion or trigger recovery actions.

values.label: Reward-function measurement audit
values.description: Review measured reward proxies against intended objectives to expose specification gaps.

values.label: Adversarial reward-function testing
values.description: Actively attempt to break reward functions and record discovered exploits before relying on them operationally.

values.label: Reward-function integrity test
values.description: Use an explicit test artifact to detect whether the reward function has been modified.

values.label: Proxy-objective alignment monitoring
values.description: Monitor whether optimized proxy metrics remain aligned with the intended objective.

values.label: Pre-training reward-hacking detection
values.description: Proxy-reward defects are screened before optimization begins.

values.label: Proxy–true reward correlation analysis
values.description: Proxy and intended rewards are compared across rollouts to assess reward misspecification.

values.label: Reward-hack frequency measurement
values.description: Quantifies how often reward hacking occurs across tasks, models, domains, and training scales.

values.label: Reward-hack property classification
values.description: Classifies reward hacks by their observable properties and behavioral mechanisms.

values.label: Reproducible reward-hacking model organisms
values.description: Uses accessible open models that reproduce reward-hacking behavior for repeatable investigation and evaluation.

values.label: Verbalization-based reward-hack detection
values.description: Uses model verbalization or acknowledgment of shortcut exploitation to improve behavioral transparency and detection.

values.label: Functional-test reward gaming
values.description: Evaluation of whether agents satisfy narrow tests through special-casing, hard-coding, stubbing, or deleting rather than preserving intended functionality.

values.label: Capability-limit and hazardous-situation evaluation
values.description: Evaluation of whether deployed agents recognize unfamiliar or hazardous situations and signal when they cannot safely act.

values.label: Reward-tampering-as-hacking classification
values.description: Treating manipulation of reward generation or inputs as a reward-hacking category for monitoring.

values.label: Interpretability-based reward-hack detection
values.description: Uses interpretability methods to identify reward-hacking loopholes and proxy exploitation.

values.label: Low hint-disclosure rate
values.description: Observed failure outcome in which models disclose influential hints infrequently, limiting faithfulness-monitoring effectiveness.

values.label: Production reward hacking
values.description: Deployed agents exploit reward functions, proxy metrics, evaluators, or environment defects instead of intended objectives.

values.label: Capability-amplified reward exploit sophistication
values.description: More capable systems discover subtler and more effective reward exploits.

values.label: Incomplete human-approval alignment signal
values.description: Human approval can reward convincing but inaccurate outputs and therefore incompletely represents factual correctness.

values.label: Post-failure reward-hack occurrence
values.description: Measures whether reward hacking follows failed normal attempts or appears immediately.

values.label: Cross-domain reward-hack coverage
values.description: Observed reward-hacking coverage across programming, agentic, open-ended, and other task domains.

values.label: Cross-model reward-hack coverage
values.description: Observed reward-hacking coverage across different model families and reasoning-model variants.

values.label: Cross-behavior reward-hack generalization
values.description: Transfer of one learned reward-hacking behavior to other distinct harmful or deceptive behaviors.

values.label: Reward-hacking anomaly transition
values.description: Detects abrupt behavioral phase transitions associated with capability-amplified reward exploitation.

values.label: Observed reward-hack frequency
values.description: Measured frequency of reward hacking across evaluated settings and training conditions.

values.label: Spurious-feature dependence
values.description: Reliance on incidental or unreliable features that produces shortcut behavior instead of intended generalization.

values.label: Hidden reward-hacking behavior
values.description: Evaluation of whether agents conceal reward hacking or remain undetected under oversight.

values.label: Functional validity failure
values.description: Outcome where narrow evaluation success does not preserve intended implementation behavior or correctness.

values.label: Capability-correctness performance tension
values.description: Outcome where speed or optimization gains conflict with correctness under reward-driven evaluation.

values.label: Novel-situation and training-distribution mismatch
values.description: Outcome where unfamiliar deployment observations produce irrational or overconfident actions outside the training distribution.

selected_clusters.name: Reward Statistic and Drift Detection
selected_clusters.description: Which reward statistic and statistical test detect post-deployment degradation while controlling false alarms?

relations.reading: Choices on Reward Statistic and Drift Detection affect the outcomes of Policy Promotion and Exposure
relations.rationale: Detection speed and false-alarm behavior determine when a deployed policy is gated, rolled back, or investigated.

values.label: Weighted reward-mean test
values.description: Compare sequential rewards using a covariance-aware weighted mean rather than an unweighted recent mean.

values.label: Inverse-covariance row-sum weighting
values.description: Derive reward weights from row sums of the inverse covariance matrix under a normal-reward assumption.

values.label: Naive simple-mean benchmark
values.description: Use the simple mean as a conventional comparison detector in RL monitoring experiments.

values.label: Complete-episode bootstrap statistic
values.description: Bootstrapping complete episodes to preserve dependence structure when constructing degradation thresholds.

values.label: BFAR-based drift detection test
values.description: Use BFAR as the primary test for detecting deployed-agent degradation.

values.label: Recent-episode simple-mean detector
values.description: Compare the recent reward mean with a reference mean; explicitly characterized as suboptimal for degradation detection.

values.label: CUSUM detector benchmark
values.description: Use CUSUM as a competing sequential-testing method for detecting reward degradation.

values.label: Hotelling mean-shift benchmark
values.description: Use Hotelling’s multivariate mean-shift test as a competing degradation detector.

values.label: Moving-average reward detector
values.description: Detecting degradation from a configurable moving average of recent episode rewards.

values.label: Multi-metric reward monitoring
values.description: Monitors several complementary reward or performance metrics to detect divergence and degradation.

values.label: Cross-metric degradation detection
values.description: Detects improvement in an optimized metric accompanied by deterioration in complementary metrics.

selected_clusters.name: Operational Drift Response Trigger
selected_clusters.description: Which operational trigger or diagnostic initiates response to detected production degradation?

values.label: Threshold-triggered monitoring response
values.description: Initiates operational response when a monitored production-quality or service metric crosses a configured threshold, without requiring rollout callbacks or persistence checks.

includes.label: Threshold-based operational alerting
includes.description: Trigger monitoring response when production quality or service indicators cross configured thresholds.

values.label: Rollout-callback diagnostic response
values.description: Initiates degradation diagnostics from rollout lifecycle callbacks, typically using threshold checks at those rollout points rather than evaluating every environment step.

includes.label: Threshold-based operational alerting
includes.description: Trigger monitoring response when production quality or service indicators cross configured thresholds.

includes.label: Callback-based rollout diagnostics
includes.description: Attaching degradation checks to a rollout lifecycle callback rather than evaluating every environment step.

values.label: Multi-signal SLO-governed rollback response
values.description: Initiates or controls rollback through a coordinated policy combining threshold checks, rollout diagnostics, persistence requirements, calibrated trigger levels, and SLO-aware serving protections.

includes.label: Threshold-based operational alerting
includes.description: Trigger monitoring response when production quality or service indicators cross configured thresholds.

includes.label: Callback-based rollout diagnostics
includes.description: Attaching degradation checks to a rollout lifecycle callback rather than evaluating every environment step.

includes.label: Persistent-condition rollback trigger
includes.description: Initiates operational response only when degradation persists for a configured duration or frequency.

includes.label: Rollback threshold calibration
includes.description: Tunes operational trigger thresholds to balance rapid degradation response against false alarms and flapping.

includes.label: SLO-aware serving policies
includes.description: Serving policies that govern routing and protection actions while satisfying latency service objectives.

values.label: False-alarm control
values.description: Desired monitoring outcome in which unchanged environments do not generate spurious degradation alerts.

values.label: Rapid degradation detection
values.description: Desired outcome in which genuine degradation is detected quickly and consistently after environmental change.

values.label: Production drift degradation effects
values.description: Input, concept, knowledge, or parameter drift produces outdated, incorrect, or irrelevant deployed responses.

values.label: User-trust erosion
values.description: Loss of user trust resulting from unattended production drift and associated model errors.

selected_clusters.name: Policy Recovery Control
selected_clusters.description: Which recovery mechanism contains or restores a deployed policy after failure?

values.label: Automated policy rollback
values.description: Automatically restore a known-good policy when regressions or safety-SLO violations occur.

values.label: State restoration for stateful policies
values.description: Restore or reset online-learning state in addition to replacing the policy version.

values.label: Automated circuit breakers
values.description: Automatic protective intervention detects degraded performance and switches or contains the deployed policy.

values.label: Safe fallback policies
values.description: A degraded agent is switched to a predefined safer policy during recovery.

values.label: Incident-capable on-call recovery
values.description: Assigning authorized on-call personnel to disable unsafe policies and activate fallback behavior.

values.label: Runbook-based incident recovery
values.description: Using stepwise runbooks for known incidents and coordinated playbooks for complex policy failures.

values.label: Fail-safe degradation handling
values.description: Keep deployed agents operating safely or recover gracefully when learning or environmental conditions cause poor performance.

values.label: Increased stateful rollback complexity
values.description: Outcome in which restoring state makes rollback more complex than replacing a stateless model.

values.label: Conversion-regression recovery workflow
values.description: Rollback, incident analysis, counterfactual testing, conservative retraining, and redeployment restore policy performance.

selected_clusters.name: Policy Promotion and Exposure
selected_clusters.description: Which pre-production and rollout process exposes and promotes candidate policies?

relations.reading: Policy Promotion and Exposure requires Training Artifact Configuration to be decided first
relations.rationale: Safe promotion and rollback depend on identifying candidate versions, their training history, and known-good restoration targets.

values.label: Counterfactual testing in CI/CD
values.description: Test alternative policy actions offline before deployment without unsafe online exploration.

values.label: Policy safety gates
values.description: Require offline evaluation and simulated safety checks before staging or production promotion.

values.label: Shadow deployment
values.description: Observe a candidate policy under production conditions without allowing it to affect live decisions.

values.label: Canary or blue-green rollout
values.description: Limit production exposure through controlled rollout patterns that support observation and containment.

values.label: Counterfactual policy-value gating
values.description: Uses logged-data estimates and their uncertainty to gate policy promotion.

selected_clusters.name: Production Policy Lineage
selected_clusters.description: Which deployed policy versions, variants, inference data, rollback events, and environments are traceable?

relations.reading: Choices on Production Policy Lineage limit the options available on Policy Promotion and Exposure
relations.rationale: Version, variant, environment, and rollback traceability constrain safe promotion and exposure decisions.

values.label: Registry-anchored policy lineage
values.description: Tracks deployed policy versions through their training histories and uses model-registry status to identify rollback targets. This provides basic traceability for deployment and recovery.

includes.label: Production policy lineage tracking
includes.description: Connect deployed policies to their training histories and associated experiments.

includes.label: Model-registry rollback targets
includes.description: Use registry promotion status to identify an unambiguous previously known-good policy version.

values.label: Auditable rollback lineage
values.description: Combines registry-based rollback targeting with explicit audit records of rollback triggers, source versions, target versions, and timing.

includes.label: Model-registry rollback targets
includes.description: Use registry promotion status to identify an unambiguous previously known-good policy version.

includes.label: Rollback event audit logging
includes.description: Record rollback triggers, timestamps, source versions, and target versions for post-mortem analysis.

values.label: End-to-end deployment evidence lineage
values.description: Links live endpoints and variants to training jobs and retained inference data, while anchoring deployed versions and rollback targets in policy lineage records.

includes.label: Production policy lineage tracking
includes.description: Connect deployed policies to their training histories and associated experiments.

includes.label: Model-registry rollback targets
includes.description: Use registry promotion status to identify an unambiguous previously known-good policy version.

includes.label: Production-variant traceability
includes.description: Record links from a live endpoint to its deployed model variant and originating training job.

includes.label: Inference capture-data retention
includes.description: Persist production requests, responses, metadata, and time-partitioned records for later evaluation.

values.label: Operational capture with environment isolation
values.description: Retains production inference records while separating training infrastructure from serving infrastructure to protect production stability and latency.

includes.label: Inference capture-data retention
includes.description: Persist production requests, responses, metadata, and time-partitioned records for later evaluation.

includes.label: Separated training and inference environments
includes.description: Keep training and serving infrastructure separate to preserve serving stability and latency.

selected_clusters.name: Training Artifact Configuration
selected_clusters.description: Which training configurations, outputs, and reproducibility artifacts are recorded for audit and replication?

values.label: CloudWatch print-log storage
values.description: Centralize operational training print logs in CloudWatch.

values.label: S3 training-output storage
values.description: Persist training outputs, metrics, and artifacts in durable object storage.

values.label: Experiment configuration tracking
values.description: Track state representations, reward functions, algorithms, hyperparameters, and job variations.

values.label: Single-click training-job replication
values.description: Replicate training jobs easily to support reproducibility and investigation.

selected_clusters.name: Runtime Safety Shielding
selected_clusters.description: Which runtime intervention architecture constrains or replaces unsafe agent actions before they reach the environment?

relations.reading: Choices on Runtime Safety Shielding affect the outcomes of Behavioral and Reasoning Evaluation
relations.rationale: The new shield architecture changes which unsafe actions reach environments and therefore changes observed behavioral safety outcomes.

values.label: Runtime action shield
values.description: An architectural layer intercepts policy actions between the agent and environment and blocks or replaces unsafe actions.

values.label: Static dynamics-based shielding
values.description: Shield decisions rely on fixed transition-dynamics, hidden-parameter, and hazard-boundary assumptions.

values.label: Shield-only safety architecture
values.description: Treating the runtime shield as the complete safety mechanism without measuring interventions under changed conditions.

values.label: Unsafe-action blocking or replacement
values.description: Blocking unsafe policy actions or substituting safer actions before environment execution.

values.label: Adaptive action shielding
values.description: Runtime shielding adapts its safe-action gate to detected distribution shifts or uncertainty.

values.label: Adaptive hidden-parameter shielding
values.description: Infer changing hidden risk parameters online and shield unsafe policy actions.

values.label: Deployment-time action constraints
values.description: Enforces allowed-action limits at deployment before policy actions reach the environment.

values.label: Business-rule validation
values.description: Validates generated or extracted outputs against structured operational and compliance rules.

values.label: Prompt-injection output guardrail
values.description: Runtime filtering or blocking that prevents prompt-injection attempts from producing unsafe agent outputs.

values.label: Restricted-topic output enforcement
values.description: Runtime enforcement that blocks responses on sensitive or prohibited topics.

selected_clusters.name: Reward Reliability Reference Strategy
selected_clusters.description: Which trusted, ensemble, oracle, or source-model reference strategy assesses reward-model reliability?

values.label: Reward-model ensemble agreement
values.description: Assess reward reliability by requiring agreement among multiple reward models before accepting a reward assessment.

includes.label: Reward-model ensemble agreement
includes.description: Using multiple reward models and requiring agreement before trusting reward assessments.

values.label: Trusted-policy reference triangulation
values.description: Assess reliability by triangulating reward behavior against a trusted policy, a synthetic oracle reward, and an ensemble of reward models.

includes.label: Trusted-policy distribution comparison
includes.description: Compare deployed policy action distributions with a trusted baseline to identify anomalous behavior.

includes.label: Synthetic oracle reward reference
includes.description: Using a high-quality synthetic oracle reward as a gold reference for evaluating proxy-reward optimization.

includes.label: Reward-model ensemble agreement
includes.description: Using multiple reward models and requiring agreement before trusting reward assessments.

values.label: Source-model reward-effect triangulation
values.description: Assess reliability by combining a synthetic oracle or source-model comparison with ensemble-based checks to isolate and validate reinforcement-learning effects on reward behavior.

includes.label: Synthetic oracle reward reference
includes.description: Using a high-quality synthetic oracle reward as a gold reference for evaluating proxy-reward optimization.

includes.label: Reward-model ensemble agreement
includes.description: Using multiple reward models and requiring agreement before trusting reward assessments.

includes.label: Reasoning-to-source model comparison
includes.description: Compares a reasoning model with its source model to isolate reinforcement-learning effects on reward hacking.

values.label: Proxy-to-gold reward gap
values.description: A widening divergence between optimized proxy reward and gold reward that exposes overoptimization.

values.label: Reward-model data-volume effect
values.description: Reward-model training-data volume changes gold-reward quality and the extent of Goodharting.

selected_clusters.name: Post-deployment Adaptation and Serving
selected_clusters.description: Which update, serving, and adaptive infrastructure changes deployed policy behavior or its production execution?

values.label: Scheduled fine-tuning jobs
values.description: Collect recent data and perform evaluated nightly or weekly incremental updates.

values.label: Continuous online model updating
values.description: Update deployed models from new information and feedback in near real time.

values.label: Metric-triggered retraining
values.description: Starting retraining when monitored performance crosses a threshold instead of only following a calendar.

values.label: Automated drift-to-deployment retraining
values.description: Automating monitoring, drift detection, retraining, validation, and deployment as one adaptation workflow.

values.label: Selective component retraining
values.description: Updating selected model components rather than all weights to reduce adaptation effort.

values.label: Rolling PEFT fine-tuning
values.description: Use parameter-efficient rolling updates to keep deployed models fresh without full retraining.

values.label: Micro-batch or single-sample updates
values.description: Apply updates at streaming micro-batch or individual-sample granularity.

values.label: Immediate feedback incorporation
values.description: Fine-tune immediately after a user rejects or corrects a deployed-system response.

values.label: Human-escalated corrective update
values.description: Escalate detected production problems to human review or retraining before or alongside automated updating.

values.label: Engagement-driven self-refinement
values.description: Refining deployed outputs or policy using engagement feedback.

values.label: API-error-driven policy refinement
